message.content:
Below you’ll find two ways to spin‑up a **Compute Engine** virtual machine that has an NVIDIA GPU attached – one uses the familiar `gcloud` CLI, the other shows what the underlying REST API call looks like so you can embed it into your own automation scripts.

---

## 1️⃣ Quick start with `gcloud`

```bash
# Pick a project ID & zone first
PROJECT_ID="my-project-id"
ZONE="us-central1-b"

# Choose a machine type that fits your workload
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-highmem-16"   # 16 vCPU + 104 GB RAM

# Pick a GPU type that’s actually sold by GCP
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a100"    # <-- replace with “nvidia-tesla-p100”, “t4” … if you really need RTX A6000 (it isn’t listed)

INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --subnet="default" \
  --network-tier="PREMIUM" \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --provisioning-model=BASIC \
  --service-account="$(gcloud iam service-accounts list --filter='displayName:(Default)' --format='value(email)')" \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --metadata=startup-script-url="" \          # Optional: add startup script here
  --disk=name="${INSTANCE_NAME}-boot-disk",
        boot=yes,
        autoDelete=yes,
        initializeParams.diskSizeGb=50,diskType=pd-balanced,imageFamily=ubuntu-2004-lts,imageProject=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --guest-cpus-per-core=1 \
  --accelerators=count=1,type=$GPU_TYPE
```

### What does each flag do?

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM profile |
| `--accelerators` | Attach a GPU (`count=1`, `type=`) |
| `--disk ... imageFamily=ubuntu-2004-lts` | Use Ubuntu 20.04 LTS base image |
| `--metadata` / `startup-script-url` | Run custom init scripts after boot |

#### Verify GPU types available in your region

```bash
gcloud compute accelerator-types list --region us-central1
```

If *RTX A6000* doesn’t appear, you’re out of luck—GCP simply hasn’t made that SKU public yet. The closest high‑end option right now is the **A100**, followed by older cards like **V100** or **T4** depending on cost vs performance trade‑offs.

---

## 2️⃣ Direct REST API Call

For those who prefer raw HTTP requests (e.g., inside Terraform, Pulumi, or a CI/CD pipeline), the same thing can be expressed as a JSON payload sent to the Compute Engine endpoint.

```json
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-project-id/zones/us-central1-b/instances
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "kind": "compute#regionInstance",
  "id": null,
  "creationTimestamp": null,
  "description": "",
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "labelFingerprint": null,

  /* ---------- Network ----------
     Default network, no special firewall rules */
  "disks": [
    {
      "deviceName": "rtx-a6000-demo",
      "index": 0,
      "mode": "READ_WRITE",
      "autoDelete": true,
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "diskType": "projects/my-project-id/zones/us-central1-b/diskTypes/pd-balanced",
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      },
      "interface": "SCSI",
      "licenses": [],
      "type": "PERSISTENT"
    }
  ],

  "machineType":
    "projects/my-project-id/zones/us-central1-b/machineTypes/n1-highmem-16",

  "metadata": { "items": [] },

  "minCpuPlatform": "",

  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "accessConfigs": [{ "natIP": "" }],
      "nicType": "GVLAN",
      "queueCount": 0,
      "stackType": "IPv4",
      "subnetwork": "global/networks/default"
    }
  ],

  "scheduling": {
    "automaticRestart": false,
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE"
  },

  "shieldedInstanceConfig": {},

  "status": "PROVISIONING",

  "labels": {},
  
  /* ---------- GPU Accelerator ----------
     Replace type with whatever GPU you have access to */
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType":
        "projects/my-project-id/zones/us-central1-b/types/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ]
}
```

### How to obtain the bearer token

Use OAuth 2.0 Service Account credentials or the `gcloud auth print-access-token` helper:

```bash
ACCESS=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @payload.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/.../instances"
```

---

## ⚠️ Important Notes

| Topic | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **GPU Availability** | As of today, GCP offers NVIDIA Tesla series (T4, P4, V100, A100…) and newer Ampere models (A10, A40, A100). An RTX A6000 is *not* publicly provisionable at this moment. Check the latest [Accelerator Types](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus) documentation. |
| **Billing** | GPUs incur extra charges per hour plus persistent storage costs. Enable billing alerts early! |
| **Region Restrictions** | Not all regions support every GPU type. Always verify with `gcloud compute accelerator-types describe`. |
| **Machine Type Limits** | Certain GPU combinations require specific machine families (e.g., `n1`, `c2`). Make sure the selected family supports the GPU count you intend. |
| **Startup Scripts** | To install drivers automatically, supply a `startup-script` metadata item pointing to a shell script that runs `sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y cuda-drivers`. |

Feel free to copy the snippets above directly into your terminal or paste them into your preferred infrastructure-as-code framework. Happy computing!
